title: Pasta e Fagioli
subtitle: Italian pasta and bean soup
excerpt: A thick, comforting Italian soup that sits somewhere between a stew and a pasta dish. Small pasta shapes are cooked directly in the bean broth so they absorb all the flavour. This is weeknight food at its best.
sourceNotes: Drawn from the classic Italian cucina povera tradition of pasta e fagioli, found across regional Italian cookbooks and home kitchens.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Add pasta fresh each time so it does not go soggy on reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bean base keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Cook pasta to order when serving.

content.text: Use small pasta shapes such as ditalini, tubetti, or broken-up spaghetti. The pasta cooks directly in the broth, so keep an eye on the liquid and top up with a splash of water if it thickens too fast.

items.prepNote: small shapes such as ditalini or tubetti

content.text: Warm the olive oil in a stockpot over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery with a pinch of salt and cook for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and rosemary sprigs and cook for 2 minutes more.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Tip in the cannellini beans and pour over the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove about a third of the beans with a ladle and roughly mash them in a bowl, then stir them back in to thicken the broth.
Remove the rosemary sprigs. Add the pasta and cook according to the packet time, stirring often. Add a splash of water if the soup thickens too much.
Season with salt and black pepper. Serve in bowls with a drizzle of olive oil and parmesan if using.

items.cause: Pasta absorbed most of the liquid
items.fix: Stir in a splash of hot water and heat through.

items.cause: Cooked too long in the broth
items.fix: Add pasta later next time; serve as soon as it is just cooked.
Add salt gradually and taste before serving.
